sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- lsp_diagnostics: Get diagnostics from configured LSP servers selected by file extension
- lsp_fix: Apply configured LSP source fixes to a file
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use lsp_diagnostics when files need diagnostics from a configured LSP server.
- Use the server parameter only when the user asks for a specific configured LSP server or multiple servers match the same extension.
- If a configured server command is missing, report the configuration error and suggest installing it or updating the server's command in pi-lsp.json.
- Use lsp_fix for files handled by a configured LSP code-action server.
- Use kind when the server needs a specific source action kind such as source.organizeImports.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: lsp_diagnostics
toolsAdded.description:
Run diagnostics using configured, language-agnostic LSP server routes.

Codemode: `tools.lsp_diagnostics(args)` resolves to a string.

paths.description: Files or directories to check. Defaults to the workspace root and routes by configured server extensions.

root.description: Workspace root for language servers. Defaults to cwd.

limit.description: Maximum files to open per selected server.

server.description: Optional configured LSP server name, or names for diagnostics. Defaults to all servers matching the file extension.

toolsAdded.name: lsp_fix
toolsAdded.description:
Apply source fixes or import organization using configured LSP server routes.

Codemode: `tools.lsp_fix(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: File to process. The server is selected from configured file extensions.

root.description: Workspace root for language servers. Defaults to cwd.

write.description: Write changed text back to the file. Defaults to false.

server.description: Optional configured LSP server name. Defaults to extension-based inference.

kind.description: Source action kind. Defaults to source.fixAll.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /usr/lib/node_modules/pi/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

"""
Fast Brainfuck interpreter in idiomatic Julia.

Compiles code to a compact IR (integer codes) with folded runs,
precomputed bracket jumps, and `[-]` → clear-cell optimization.
Executes on a 30000-cell `UInt8` tape with wraparound arithmetic.
"""

# ── IR instruction codes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const NOP       = 0
const INCR      = 1
const DECR      = 2
const ADVANCE   = 3
const RETREAT   = 4
const OUTPUT    = 5
const INPUT     = 6
const JZ_FWD    = 7   # jump forward if cell == 0
const JZ_BWD    = 8   # jump backward if cell == 0
const CLEAR     = 9   # clear-cell: `[-]`

# ── Compiler ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}

Compile Brainfuck source into a compact integer-encoded IR.

Optimisations:
- Fold consecutive `+`/`-`/`<`/`>` into single instructions
- Precompute matching bracket jumps
- Replace `[-]` with a single CLEAR instruction
"""
function compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}
    n = length(code)
    # First pass: find matching brackets
    jump = Dict{Int, Int}()
    stack = Int[]
    for i in 1:n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '['
            push!(stack, i)
        elseif c == ']'
            if isempty(stack)
                error("Brainfuck: unmatched `]` at position $(i)")
            end
            j = pop!(stack)
            jump[i] = j   # `]` → `[`
            jump[j] = i   # `[` → `]`
        end
    end
    if !isempty(stack)
        error("Brainfuck: unmatched `[` at position $(stack[end])")
    end

    # Second pass: emit IR with folding
    buf = Int[]
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '+'
            dir = +1; tag = INCR
        elseif c == '-'
            dir = -1; tag = DECR
        elseif c == '<'
            dir = -1; tag = ADVANCE
        elseif c == '>'
            dir = +1; tag = RETREAT
        else
            push!(buf, tag_from_char(c))
            i += 1; continue
        end

        # Fold consecutive same-direction moves
        count = 1
        while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
            count += 1
        end
        push!(buf, tag)
        push!(buf, count)   # operand: magnitude
        i += count

        # Detect `[-]` pattern: DECR followed by `]`
        if tag == DECR && i <= n && code[i] == ']'
            # Check that the next char after `]` is nothing or a non-bracket
            # (i.e. the `]` is not part of a larger construct)
            push!(buf, CLEAR)
            push!(buf, 0)      # operand unused
            i += 1             # skip the `]`
        end
    end
    return buf
end

# Map non-movement, non-bracket chars to IR codes
tag_from_char(c::Char) = c == '.' ? OUTPUT : c == ',' ? INPUT : NOP


# ── Interpreter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String

Execute compiled Brainfuck code and return output as a `String`.

- Tape: 30000 cells, `UInt8` with wraparound (`0x00 ± n` mod `0x100`)
- Errors: `BoundsError` for unmatched brackets (caught in compile)
            `BoundsError` for pointer leaving tape
"""
function run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String
    ir = compile(code)
    tape = zeros(UInt8, 30000)
    ptr = 1
    ip = 1
    n_ir = length(ir)
    out_buf = IOBuffer()
    inp = input
    inp_pos = 1

    while ip <= n_ir
        tag = ir[ip]
        if tag == NOP
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INCR
            tape[ptr] += ir[ip + 1]   # fold count
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == DECR
            tape[ptr] -= ir[ip + 1]   # fold count
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == ADVANCE
            ptr -= ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == RETREAT
            ptr += ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == OUTPUT
            write(out_buf, Char(tape[ptr]))
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INPUT
            if inp_pos <= length(inp)
                tape[ptr] = UInt8(inp[inp_pos])
                inp_pos += 1
            else
                tape[ptr] = 0  # EOF → 0
            end
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == JZ_FWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == JZ_BWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == CLEAR
            tape[ptr] = 0x00
            ip += 2
        else
            error("Brainfuck: unknown IR tag $tag")
        end
    end
    return String(take!(out_buf))
end


# ── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# "Hello World!" — classic
hello = "++++++++[>++++[>++>+++>+++>+<<<<-]>+>+>->>+[<]<-]>>.>---.+++++++..+++.>>.<-.<.+++.------.--------.>>+.>++."

# Echo: reads one byte and outputs it
echo = ","
echo_prog = ","  # read one byte, implicitly output? No — need "."
echo_full = ",."

# Simple loop: output 'A' (65) 5 times
five_a = "+[.>++++++++[<++++++++>-]<.]"

# Clear tape test: `[-]` on a cell set to 1
clear_test = "+[-]"

# Unmatched bracket error
unmatched = "[++"

# Pointer out-of-bounds error
ptr_err = ">>>"

function run_tests()
    println("=== Brainfuck Tests ===\n")

    # Test 1: Hello World
    result = run_bf(hello)
    @assert result == "Hello World!\n" "Hello World failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Hello World!")

    # Test 2: Echo (read a byte, output it)
    result = run_bf(echo_full, "X")
    @assert result == "X" "Echo failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Echo")

    # Test 3: Read input character
    result = run_bf(",", "42")
    @assert result == "4" "Read input failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Read input")

    # Test 4: Five A's
    result = run_bf(five_a)
    @assert result == "AAAAA" "Five A failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Five A's")

    # Test 5: Clear cell
    result = run_bf(clear_test)
    @assert result == "" "Clear cell failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Clear cell `[-]`")

    # Test 6: Unmatched bracket → error
    try
        run_bf(unmatched)
        error("Should have errored on unmatched bracket")
    catch e
        @assert occursin("unmatched", lowercase(string(e))) "Wrong error message: $e"
    end
    println("✓ Unmatched bracket error")

    # Test 7: Pointer out of bounds → error
    try
        run_bf(ptr_err)
        error("Should have errored on pointer overflow")
    catch e
        @assert occursin("pointer", lowercase(string(e))) "Wrong error message: $e"
    end
    println("✓ Pointer out-of-bounds error")

    # Test 8: Wraparound arithmetic
    # Set cell to 0, then decrement → 255
    wrap = "+[-]>+[-]<+[-]>+[.]"
    result = run_bf(wrap)
    @assert result == "ÿ" "Wraparound failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Wraparound (decrement 0 → 255)")

    # Test 9: Folded runs
    # 255 '+' folded to a single INCR with operand 255
    folded = "+" ^ 255
    result = run_bf(folded)
    @assert result == "" "Folded 255 '+' failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Folded runs (255 × '+')")

    # Test 10: F-Prime (Fibonacci)
    fprime = "++++++++[>++++[>++>+++>+++>+<<<<-]>+>+>->>+[<]<-]>>.>---.+++++++..+++.>>.<-.<.+++.------.--------.>>+.>++."
    result = run_bf(fprime)
    @assert result == "Hello World!\n" "F-Prime failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ F-Prime = Hello World!")

    println("\n=== All tests passed ===")
end

if abspath(PROGRAM_FILE) == @__FILE__
    run_tests()
end

"""
Fast Brainfuck interpreter in idiomatic Julia.

Compiles code to a compact IR (integer codes) with folded runs,
precomputed bracket jumps, and `[-]` → clear-cell optimization.
Executes on a 30000-cell `UInt8` tape with wraparound arithmetic.
"""

# ── IR instruction codes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const NOP       = 0
const INCR      = 1
const DECR      = 2
const ADVANCE   = 3
const RETREAT   = 4
const OUTPUT    = 5
const INPUT     = 6
const JZ_FWD    = 7   # jump forward if cell == 0
const JZ_BWD    = 8   # jump backward if cell == 0
const CLEAR     = 9   # clear-cell: `[-]`

# ── Compiler ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}

Compile Brainfuck source into a compact integer-encoded IR.

Optimisations:
- Fold consecutive `+`/`-`/`<`/`>` into single instructions
- Precompute matching bracket jumps
- Replace `[-]` with a single CLEAR instruction
"""
function compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}
    n = length(code)
    # First pass: find matching brackets
    jump = Dict{Int, Int}()
    stack = Int[]
    for i in 1:n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '['
            push!(stack, i)
        elseif c == ']'
            if isempty(stack)
                error("Brainfuck: unmatched `]` at position $(i)")
            end
            j = pop!(stack)
            jump[i] = j   # `]` → `[`
            jump[j] = i   # `[` → `]`
        end
    end
    if !isempty(stack)
        error("Brainfuck: unmatched `[` at position $(stack[end])")
    end

    # Second pass: emit IR with folding
    buf = Int[]
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '+'
            dir = +1; tag = INCR
        elseif c == '-'
            dir = -1; tag = DECR
        elseif c == '<'
            dir = -1; tag = ADVANCE
        elseif c == '>'
            dir = +1; tag = RETREAT
        else
            push!(buf, tag_from_char(c))
            i += 1; continue
        end

        # Fold consecutive same-direction moves
        count = 1
        while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
            count += 1
        end
        push!(buf, tag)
        push!(buf, count)   # operand: magnitude
        i += count


    end
    return buf
end

# Map non-movement, non-bracket chars to IR codes
tag_from_char(c::Char) = c == '.' ? OUTPUT : c == ',' ? INPUT : NOP


# ── Interpreter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String

Execute compiled Brainfuck code and return output as a `String`.

- Tape: 30000 cells, `UInt8` with wraparound (`0x00 ± n` mod `0x100`)
- Errors: `BoundsError` for unmatched brackets (caught in compile)
            `BoundsError` for pointer leaving tape
"""
function run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String
    ir = compile(code)
    tape = zeros(UInt8, 30000)
    ptr = 1
    ip = 1
    n_ir = length(ir)
    out_buf = IOBuffer()
    inp = input
    inp_pos = 1

    while ip <= n_ir
        tag = ir[ip]
        if tag == NOP
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INCR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) + ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == DECR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) - ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == ADVANCE
            ptr -= ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == RETREAT
            ptr += ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == OUTPUT
            write(out_buf, Char(tape[ptr]))
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INPUT
            if inp_pos <= length(inp)
                tape[ptr] = UInt8(inp[inp_pos])
                inp_pos += 1
            else
                tape[ptr] = 0  # EOF → 0
            end
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == JZ_FWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == JZ_BWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == CLEAR
            tape[ptr] = 0x00
            ip += 2
        else
            error("Brainfuck: unknown IR tag $tag")
        end
    end
    return String(take!(out_buf))
end

    # First pass: find matching brackets (source positions)
    jump_src = Dict{Int, Int}()   # source_pos → source_pos
    stack = Int[]
    for i in 1:n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '['
            push!(stack, i)
        elseif c == ']'
            if isempty(stack)
                error("Brainfuck: unmatched `]` at position $(i)")
            end
            j = pop!(stack)
            jump_src[i] = j   # `]` → `[`
            jump_src[j] = i   # `[` → `]`
        end
    end
    if !isempty(stack)
        error("Brainfuck: unmatched `[` at position $(stack[end])")
    end

    # Second pass: simulate emit to compute IR positions for each bracket
    # ir_pos[i] = IR position of source character at position i
    ir_pos = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    ip = 1
    for i in 1:n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '[' || c == ']'
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 2   # tag + operand
        elseif c in ("+", "-", "<", ">")
            # Will be folded; record placeholder
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 2   # placeholder
        else
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 1   # NOP / OUTPUT / INPUT
        end
    end

    # Third pass: emit IR
    buf = Int[]
    ip = 1
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '+'
            tag = INCR
        elseif c == '-'
            tag = DECR
        elseif c == '<'
            tag = ADVANCE
        elseif c == '>'
            tag = RETREAT
        elseif c == '['
            # Emit JZ_BWD targeting the matching `]`
            push!(buf, JZ_BWD)
            push!(buf, ir_pos[jump_src[i]])   # target = IR pos of `]`
            ip += 2
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == ']'
            # Emit JZ_FWD targeting the matching `[`
            push!(buf, JZ_FWD)
            push!(buf, ir_pos[jump_src[i]])   # target = IR pos of `[`
            ip += 2
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == '.'
            push!(buf, OUTPUT)
            ip += 1
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == ','
            push!(buf, INPUT)
            ip += 1
            i += 1; continue
        else
            # NOP (space, etc.)
            push!(buf, NOP)
            ip += 1
            i += 1; continue
        end

        # Fold consecutive same-direction moves
        count = 1
        while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
            count += 1
        end
        push!(buf, tag)
        push!(buf, count)   # operand: magnitude
        ip += 2
        i += count

        # Detect `[-]` pattern: DECR followed by `]`
        if tag == DECR && i <= n && code[i] == ']'
            push!(buf, CLEAR)
            push!(buf, 0)      # operand unused
            ip += 2
            i += 1             # skip the `]`
        end
    end
    return buf
end


# ── Interpreter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String

Execute compiled Brainfuck code and return output as a `String`.

- Tape: 30000 cells, `UInt8` with wraparound (`0x00 ± n` mod `0x100`)
- Errors: `BoundsError` for unmatched brackets (caught in compile)
            `BoundsError` for pointer leaving tape
"""
function run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String
    ir = compile(code)
    tape = zeros(UInt8, 30000)
    ptr = 1
    ip = 1
    n_ir = length(ir)
    out_buf = IOBuffer()
    inp = input
    inp_pos = 1

    while ip <= n_ir
        tag = ir[ip]
        if tag == NOP
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INCR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) + ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == DECR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) - ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == ADVANCE
            ptr -= ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == RETREAT
            ptr += ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == OUTPUT
            write(out_buf, Char(tape[ptr]))
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INPUT
            if inp_pos <= length(inp)
                tape[ptr] = UInt8(inp[inp_pos])
                inp_pos += 1
            else
                tape[ptr] = 0  # EOF → 0
            end
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == JZ_FWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == JZ_BWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == CLEAR
            tape[ptr] = 0x00
            ip += 2
        else
            error("Brainfuck: unknown IR tag $tag")
        end
    end
    return String(take!(out_buf))
end

"""
Fast Brainfuck interpreter in idiomatic Julia.

Compiles code to a compact IR (integer codes) with folded runs,
precomputed bracket jumps, and `[-]` → clear-cell optimization.
Executes on a 30000-cell `UInt8` tape with wraparound arithmetic.
"""

# ── IR instruction codes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const NOP       = 0
const INCR      = 1
const DECR      = 2
const ADVANCE   = 3
const RETREAT   = 4
const OUTPUT    = 5
const INPUT     = 6
const JZ_FWD    = 7   # jump forward if cell == 0
const JZ_BWD    = 8   # jump backward if cell == 0
const CLEAR     = 9   # clear-cell: `[-]`

# ── Compiler ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}

Compile Brainfuck source into a compact integer-encoded IR.

Optimisations:
- Fold consecutive `+`/`-`/`<`/`>` into single instructions
- Precompute matching bracket jumps
- Replace `[-]` with a single CLEAR instruction
"""
function compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}
    n = length(code)
    if n == 0
        return Int[]
    end

    # First pass: find matching brackets (source positions)
    jump_src = Dict{Int, Int}()   # source_pos → source_pos
    stack = Int[]
    for i in 1:n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '['
            push!(stack, i)
        elseif c == ']'
            if isempty(stack)
                error("Brainfuck: unmatched `]` at position $(i)")
            end
            j = pop!(stack)
            jump_src[i] = j   # `]` → `[`
            jump_src[j] = i   # `[` → `]`
        end
    end
    if !isempty(stack)
        error("Brainfuck: unmatched `[` at position $(stack[end])")
    end

    # Second pass: simulate full emit (including folding & [-] opt) to
    # record the IR position of every source character.
    # ir_pos[i] = IR position of source char at position i
    ir_pos = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    ip = 1
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c in ('+', '-', '<', '>')
            # Fold
            count = 1
            while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
                count += 1
            end
            # Emit placeholder: tag + operand
            for k in 1:count
                ir_pos[i + k - 1] = ip
            end
            ip += 2
            i += count
            # Check [-] optimization
            if c == '-' && i <= n && code[i] == ']'
                # Only if char before the `-` run is `[`
                if i - count >= 1 && code[i - count] == '['
                    # Emit CLEAR (2 elements)
                    for k in 1:1
                        ir_pos[i + k - 1] = ip
                    end
                    ip += 2
                    i += 1
                end
            end
        elseif c == '[' || c == ']'
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 2
            i += 1
        else
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 1
            i += 1
        end
    end

    # Third pass: emit IR
    buf = Int[]
    ip = 1
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '+'
            tag = INCR
        elseif c == '-'
            tag = DECR
        elseif c == '<'
            tag = ADVANCE
        elseif c == '>'
            tag = RETREAT
        elseif c == '['
            # JZ_BWD targeting the matching `]`
            push!(buf, JZ_BWD)
            push!(buf, ir_pos[jump_src[i]])
            ip += 2
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == ']'
            # JZ_FWD targeting the matching `[`
            push!(buf, JZ_FWD)
            push!(buf, ir_pos[jump_src[i]])
            ip += 2
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == '.'
            push!(buf, OUTPUT)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        elseif c == ','
            push!(buf, INPUT)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        else
            push!(buf, NOP)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        end

        # Fold consecutive same-direction moves
        count = 1
        while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
            count += 1
        end
        push!(buf, tag)
        push!(buf, count)
        ip += 2
        i += count

        # [-] optimization: `[` immediately before `-` run, `]` immediately after
        if tag == DECR && i <= n && code[i] == ']'
            if i - count >= 1 && code[i - count] == '['
                push!(buf, CLEAR)
                push!(buf, 0)
                ip += 2
                i += 1
            end
        end
    end
    return buf
end


# ── Interpreter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String

Execute compiled Brainfuck code and return output as a `String`.

- Tape: 30000 cells, `UInt8` with wraparound (`0x00 ± n` mod `0x100`)
- Errors: `BoundsError` for unmatched brackets (caught in compile)
            `BoundsError` for pointer leaving tape
"""
function run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String
    ir = compile(code)
    tape = zeros(UInt8, 30000)
    ptr = 1
    ip = 1
    n_ir = length(ir)
    out_buf = IOBuffer()
    inp = input
    inp_pos = 1

    while ip <= n_ir
        tag = ir[ip]
        if tag == NOP
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INCR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) + ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == DECR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) - ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == ADVANCE
            ptr -= ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == RETREAT
            ptr += ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == OUTPUT
            write(out_buf, Char(tape[ptr]))
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INPUT
            if inp_pos <= length(inp)
                tape[ptr] = UInt8(inp[inp_pos])
                inp_pos += 1
            else
                tape[ptr] = 0  # EOF → 0
            end
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == JZ_FWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == JZ_BWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == CLEAR
            tape[ptr] = 0x00
            ip += 2
        else
            error("Brainfuck: unknown IR tag $tag")
        end
    end
    return String(take!(out_buf))
end


# ── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# "Hello World!" — classic
hello = "++++++++[>++++[>++>+++>+++>+<<<<-]>+>+>->>+[<]<-]>>.>---.+++++++..+++.>>.<-.<.+++.------.--------.>>+.>++."

# Echo: reads one byte and outputs it
echo_full = ",."

# Simple loop: output 'A' (65) 5 times
five_a = "+[.>++++++++[<++++++++>-]<.]"

# Clear tape test: `[-]` on a cell set to 1
clear_test = "+[-]"

# Unmatched bracket error
unmatched = "[++"

# Pointer out-of-bounds error
ptr_err = ">>>"

function run_tests()
    println("=== Brainfuck Tests ===\n")

    # Test 1: Hello World
    result = run_bf(hello)
    @assert result == "Hello World!\n" "Hello World failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Hello World!")

    # Test 2: Echo (read a byte, output it)
    result = run_bf(echo_full, "X")
    @assert result == "X" "Echo failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Echo")

    # Test 3: Read input character
    result = run_bf(",", "42")
    @assert result == "4" "Read input failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Read input")

    # Test 4: Five A's
    result = run_bf(five_a)
    @assert result == "AAAAA" "Five A failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Five A's")

    # Test 5: Clear cell
    result = run_bf(clear_test)
    @assert result == "" "Clear cell failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Clear cell `[-]`")

    # Test 6: Unmatched bracket → error
    try
        run_bf(unmatched)
        error("Should have errored on unmatched bracket")
    catch e
        @assert occursin("unmatched", lowercase(string(e))) "Wrong error message: $e"
    end
    println("✓ Unmatched bracket error")

    # Test 7: Pointer out of bounds → error
    try
        run_bf(ptr_err)
        error("Should have errored on pointer overflow")
    catch e
        @assert occursin("pointer", lowercase(string(e))) "Wrong error message: $e"
    end
    println("✓ Pointer out-of-bounds error")

    # Test 8: Wraparound arithmetic
    wrap = "+[-]>+[-]<+[-]>+[.]"
    result = run_bf(wrap)
    @assert result == "ÿ" "Wraparound failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Wraparound (decrement 0 → 255)")

    # Test 9: Folded runs
    folded = "+" ^ 255
    result = run_bf(folded)
    @assert result == "" "Folded 255 '+' failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Folded runs (255 × '+')")

    # Test 10: F-Prime (Fibonacci)
    fprime = "++++++++[>++++[>++>+++>+++>+<<<<-]>+>+>->>+[<]<-]>>.>---.+++++++..+++.>>.<-.<.+++.------.--------.>>+.>++."
    result = run_bf(fprime)
    @assert result == "Hello World!\n" "F-Prime failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ F-Prime = Hello World!")

    println("\n=== All tests passed ===")
end

if abspath(PROGRAM_FILE) == @__FILE__
    run_tests()
end

"""
Fast Brainfuck interpreter in idiomatic Julia.

Compiles code to a compact IR (integer codes) with folded runs,
precomputed bracket jumps, and `[-]` → clear-cell optimization.
Executes on a 30000-cell `UInt8` tape with wraparound arithmetic.
"""

# ── IR instruction codes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const NOP       = 0
const INCR      = 1
const DECR      = 2
const ADVANCE   = 3
const RETREAT   = 4
const OUTPUT    = 5
const INPUT     = 6
const JZ_FWD    = 7   # `]`: if cell != 0 jump back to loop start; else exit
const JZ_BWD    = 8   # `[`: if cell == 0 jump to after `]`; else continue
const CLEAR     = 9   # clear-cell: `[-]`

# ── Compiler ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}

Compile Brainfuck source into a compact integer-encoded IR.

Optimisations:
- Fold consecutive `+`/`-`/`<`/`>` into single instructions
- Precompute matching bracket jumps
- Replace `[-]` with a single CLEAR instruction
"""
function compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}
    n = length(code)
    if n == 0
        return Int[]
    end

    # First pass: find matching brackets (source positions)
    jump_src = Dict{Int, Int}()
    stack = Int[]
    for i in 1:n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '['
            push!(stack, i)
        elseif c == ']'
            if isempty(stack)
                error("Brainfuck: unmatched `]` at position $(i)")
            end
            j = pop!(stack)
            jump_src[i] = j
            jump_src[j] = i
        end
    end
    if !isempty(stack)
        error("Brainfuck: unmatched `[` at position $(stack[end])")
    end

    # Second pass: simulate full emit (including folding & [-] opt) to
    # record the IR position of every source character.
    ir_pos = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    ip = 1
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c in ('+', '-', '<', '>')
            count = 1
            while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
                count += 1
            end
            for k in 1:count
                ir_pos[i + k - 1] = ip
            end
            ip += 2
            i += count
            # [-] optimization
            if c == '-' && i <= n && code[i] == ']'
                if i - count >= 1 && code[i - count] == '['
                    for k in 1:1
                        ir_pos[i + k - 1] = ip
                    end
                    ip += 2
                    i += 1
                end
            end
        elseif c == '[' || c == ']'
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 2
            i += 1
        else
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 1
            i += 1
        end
    end

    # Third pass: emit IR
    buf = Int[]
    ip = 1
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '+'
            tag = INCR
        elseif c == '-'
            tag = DECR
        elseif c == '<'
            tag = ADVANCE
        elseif c == '>'
            tag = RETREAT
        elseif c == '['
            push!(buf, JZ_BWD)
            push!(buf, ir_pos[jump_src[i]] + 2)
            ip += 2
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == ']'
            push!(buf, JZ_FWD)
            push!(buf, ir_pos[jump_src[i]] + 2)
            ip += 2
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == '.'
            push!(buf, OUTPUT)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        elseif c == ','
            push!(buf, INPUT)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        else
            push!(buf, NOP)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        end

        count = 1
        while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
            count += 1
        end
        push!(buf, tag)
        push!(buf, count)
        ip += 2
        i += count

        if tag == DECR && i <= n && code[i] == ']'
            if i - count >= 1 && code[i - count] == '['
                push!(buf, CLEAR)
                push!(buf, 0)
                ip += 2
                i += 1
            end
        end
    end
    return buf
end


# ── Interpreter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String

Execute compiled Brainfuck code and return output as a `String`.

- Tape: 30000 cells, `UInt8` with wraparound (`0x00 ± n` mod `0x100`)
- Errors: `BoundsError` for unmatched brackets (caught in compile)
            `BoundsError` for pointer leaving tape
"""
function run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String
    ir = compile(code)
    tape = zeros(UInt8, 30000)
    ptr = 1
    ip = 1
    n_ir = length(ir)
    out_buf = IOBuffer()
    inp = input
    inp_pos = 1

    while ip <= n_ir
        tag = ir[ip]
        if tag == NOP
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INCR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) + ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == DECR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) - ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == ADVANCE
            ptr -= ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == RETREAT
            ptr += ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == OUTPUT
            write(out_buf, Char(tape[ptr]))
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INPUT
            if inp_pos <= length(inp)
                tape[ptr] = UInt8(inp[inp_pos])
                inp_pos += 1
            else
                tape[ptr] = 0
            end
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == JZ_FWD
            if tape[ptr] != 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == JZ_BWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == CLEAR
            tape[ptr] = 0x00
            ip += 2
        else
            error("Brainfuck: unknown IR tag $tag")
        end
    end
    return String(take!(out_buf))
end

"""
Fast Brainfuck interpreter in idiomatic Julia.

Compiles code to a compact IR (integer codes) with folded runs,
precomputed bracket jumps, and `[-]` → clear-cell optimization.
Executes on a 30000-cell `UInt8` tape with wraparound arithmetic.
"""

# ── IR instruction codes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const NOP       = 0
const INCR      = 1
const DECR      = 2
const ADVANCE   = 3
const RETREAT   = 4
const OUTPUT    = 5
const INPUT     = 6
const JZ_FWD    = 7   # `]`: if cell != 0 jump back to loop start; else exit
const JZ_BWD    = 8   # `[`: if cell == 0 jump to after `]`; else continue
const CLEAR     = 9   # clear-cell: `[-]`

# ── Compiler ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}

Compile Brainfuck source into a compact integer-encoded IR.

Optimisations:
- Fold consecutive `+`/`-`/`<`/`>` into single instructions
- Precompute matching bracket jumps
- Replace `[-]` with a single CLEAR instruction
"""
function compile(code::AbstractString)::Vector{Int}
    n = length(code)
    if n == 0
        return Int[]
    end

    # First pass: find matching brackets (source positions)
    jump_src = Dict{Int, Int}()
    stack = Int[]
    for i in 1:n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '['
            push!(stack, i)
        elseif c == ']'
            if isempty(stack)
                error("Brainfuck: unmatched `]` at position $(i)")
            end
            j = pop!(stack)
            jump_src[i] = j
            jump_src[j] = i
        end
    end
    if !isempty(stack)
        error("Brainfuck: unmatched `[` at position $(stack[end])")
    end

    # Second pass: simulate full emit (including folding & [-] opt) to
    # record the IR position of every source character.
    ir_pos = Vector{Int}(undef, n)
    ip = 1
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c in ('+', '-', '<', '>')
            count = 1
            while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
                count += 1
            end
            for k in 1:count
                ir_pos[i + k - 1] = ip
            end
            ip += 2
            i += count
            # [-] optimization
            if c == '-' && i <= n && code[i] == ']'
                if i - count - 1 >= 1 && code[i - count - 1] == '['
                    for k in 1:1
                        ir_pos[i + k - 1] = ip
                    end
                    ip += 2
                    i += 1
                end
            end
        elseif c == '[' || c == ']'
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 2
            i += 1
        else
            ir_pos[i] = ip
            ip += 1
            i += 1
        end
    end

    # Third pass: emit IR
    buf = Int[]
    ip = 1
    i = 1
    while i <= n
        c = code[i]
        if c == '+'
            tag = INCR
        elseif c == '-'
            tag = DECR
        elseif c == '<'
            tag = ADVANCE
        elseif c == '>'
            tag = RETREAT
        elseif c == '['
            push!(buf, JZ_BWD)
            push!(buf, ir_pos[jump_src[i]] + 2)
            ip += 2
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == ']'
            push!(buf, JZ_FWD)
            push!(buf, ir_pos[jump_src[i]] + 2)
            ip += 2
            i += 1; continue
        elseif c == '.'
            push!(buf, OUTPUT)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        elseif c == ','
            push!(buf, INPUT)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        else
            push!(buf, NOP)
            ip += 1; i += 1; continue
        end

        count = 1
        while i + count <= n && code[i + count] == c
            count += 1
        end
        push!(buf, tag)
        push!(buf, count)
        ip += 2
        i += count

        if tag == DECR && i <= n && code[i] == ']'
            if i - count - 1 >= 1 && code[i - count - 1] == '['
                push!(buf, CLEAR)
                push!(buf, 0)
                ip += 2
                i += 1
            end
        end
    end
    return buf
end


# ── Interpreter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
    run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String

Execute compiled Brainfuck code and return output as a `String`.

- Tape: 30000 cells, `UInt8` with wraparound (`0x00 ± n` mod `0x100`)
- Errors: `BoundsError` for unmatched brackets (caught in compile)
            `BoundsError` for pointer leaving tape
"""
function run_bf(code::AbstractString, input::AbstractString="")::String
    ir = compile(code)
    tape = zeros(UInt8, 30000)
    ptr = 1
    ip = 1
    n_ir = length(ir)
    out_buf = IOBuffer()
    inp = input
    inp_pos = 1

    while ip <= n_ir
        tag = ir[ip]
        if tag == NOP
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INCR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) + ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == DECR
            tape[ptr] = UInt8(mod(Int(tape[ptr]) - ir[ip + 1], 256))
            ip += 2
        elseif tag == ADVANCE
            ptr -= ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == RETREAT
            ptr += ir[ip + 1]
            ip += 2
            if ptr < 1 || ptr > 30000
                error("Brainfuck: pointer left tape ($ptr)")
            end
        elseif tag == OUTPUT
            write(out_buf, Char(tape[ptr]))
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == INPUT
            if inp_pos <= length(inp)
                tape[ptr] = UInt8(inp[inp_pos])
                inp_pos += 1
            else
                tape[ptr] = 0
            end
            ip += 1
        elseif tag == JZ_FWD
            if tape[ptr] != 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == JZ_BWD
            if tape[ptr] == 0
                ip = ir[ip + 1]
            else
                ip += 2
            end
        elseif tag == CLEAR
            tape[ptr] = 0x00
            ip += 2
        else
            error("Brainfuck: unknown IR tag $tag")
        end
    end
    return String(take!(out_buf))
end


# ── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# "Hello World!" — classic
hello = "++++++++[>++++[>++>+++>+++>+<<<<-]>+>+>->>+[<]<-]>>.>---.+++++++..+++.>>.<-.<.+++.------.--------.>>+.>++."

# Echo: reads one byte and outputs it
echo_full = ",."

# Output 'A' (65) once: 9*7+2 = 65
prog_a = "+++++++++[>+++++++<-]>++."

# Clear tape test: `[-]` on a cell set to 1
clear_test = "+[-]"

# Unmatched bracket error
unmatched = "[++"

# Pointer out-of-bounds error
ptr_err = ">>>"

function run_tests()
    println("=== Brainfuck Tests ===\n")

    # Test 1: Hello World
    result = run_bf(hello)
    @assert result == "Hello World!\n" "Hello World failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Hello World!")

    # Test 2: Echo (read a byte, output it)
    result = run_bf(echo_full, "X")
    @assert result == "X" "Echo failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Echo")

    # Test 3: Read input character (read + output)
    result = run_bf(",.", "42")
    @assert result == "4" "Read input failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Read input")

    # Test 4: Output 'A' (65)
    result = run_bf(prog_a)
    @assert result == "A" "Output A failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Output 'A'")

    # Test 5: Clear cell
    result = run_bf(clear_test)
    @assert result == "" "Clear cell failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Clear cell `[-]`")

    # Test 6: Unmatched bracket → error
    try
        run_bf(unmatched)
        error("Should have errored on unmatched bracket")
    catch e
        @assert occursin("unmatched", lowercase(string(e))) "Wrong error message: $e"
    end
    println("✓ Unmatched bracket error")

    # Test 7: Pointer out of bounds → error
    try
        run_bf(ptr_err)
        error("Should have errored on pointer overflow")
    catch e
        @assert occursin("pointer", lowercase(string(e))) "Wrong error message: $e"
    end
    println("✓ Pointer out-of-bounds error")

    # Test 8: Wraparound arithmetic
    wrap = "[-]-."
    result = run_bf(wrap)
    @assert result == "ÿ" "Wraparound failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Wraparound (decrement 0 → 255)")

    # Test 9: Folded runs
    folded = "+" ^ 255
    result = run_bf(folded)
    @assert result == "" "Folded 255 '+' failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ Folded runs (255 × '+')")

    # Test 10: F-Prime (Fibonacci)
    fprime = "++++++++[>++++[>++>+++>+++>+<<<<-]>+>+>->>+[<]<-]>>.>---.+++++++..+++.>>.<-.<.+++.------.--------.>>+.>++."
    result = run_bf(fprime)
    @assert result == "Hello World!\n" "F-Prime failed: got $(repr(result))"
    println("✓ F-Prime = Hello World!")

    println("\n=== All tests passed ===")
end

if abspath(PROGRAM_FILE) == @__FILE__
    run_tests()
end
